name: Practice (abhyāsa)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: if one cannot hold the thought (citta) steadily fixed on the Lord, one should seek to reach him by the yoga of practice (abhyāsa-yoga) (12.9) — the second of the graded means of 12.8–11; for one incapable even of practice, work for the Lord is offered instead (12.10); in the ranking of 12.12 knowledge is better than practice. The verses do not describe the practice further; elsewhere the text uses abhyāsa for bringing the wandering mind back again and again (6.26, 6.35) and speaks of a 'yoga of practice' with thought (cetas) not going to anything else (8.8).

prerequisites: The text addresses it to one not able to fix citta steadily on the Lord (12.9).
notes: Chs. 10–12 contribution, combining extractor A's prc:abhyasa and extractor B's prc:abhyasa-yoga. 12.9 names practice only; practice with dispassion (prc:abhyasa-vairagya, 6.35) is not mentioned here.

name: Undivided devotion (ananya-bhakti)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Devotion to the Lord alone: doing his work, holding him supreme, being devoted, free from attachment, without enmity toward any being (11.55); fixing the mind (manas) on him and worshipping him, ever yoked, with supreme faith (12.2); laying down all actions in him, holding him supreme, meditating on him with undivided yoga (12.6). By it alone the Lord can be known, seen and entered in truth (11.54); he soon delivers such devotees from the ocean of death and saṃsāra (12.7).

name: Worship of the imperishable unmanifest (akṣara / avyakta upāsanā)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Worshipping the imperishable — indefinable, unmanifest, all-pervading, unthinkable, unchanging, immovable, constant — while restraining the whole group of the senses, being even in understanding everywhere and delighting in the welfare of all beings; such worshippers also reach the Lord (12.3–4).
prerequisites: restraint of the whole group of the senses (12.4)
delight in the welfare of all beings (12.4)

warnings.text: Greater is the hardship of those whose awareness (cetas) is attached to the unmanifest; for the unmanifest goal is reached with difficulty by the embodied.

notes: New practice for 12.3–5, combining extractor A's prc:avyakta-upasana and extractor B's prc:worship-of-the-imperishable-unmanifest. Commentators identify the object differently: Śaṅkara as brahman beyond all attributes, Rāmānuja as the individual self's own nature (recalled; see dsp:bhagavad-gita-lord-or-unmanifest); the text names it only akṣara and avyakta.

name: Mantra repetition (japa)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: 'Of sacrifices I am the sacrifice of japa' (10.25): muttered recitation counted as a sacrifice and named as the Lord's manifestation among sacrifices; in the same verse the Lord is 'the one syllable' among utterances.

name: Relinquishing the fruit of all actions
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: If unable to do even the Lord's work: resorting to his yoga, self-restrained, relinquish the fruit of all actions (12.11). It is then ranked above meditation (which is above knowledge, which is above practice), and peace follows relinquishment immediately (12.12).

name: Devotional singing of the Lord's names and deeds (kīrtana, saṅkīrtana)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: with their thought (citta) on the Lord and their life-breaths gone into him, the devotees awaken one another and are always speaking of him (bodhayantaḥ parasparaṃ kathayantaś ca mām), and are content and delight; to those who so worship with love he gives the yoga of understanding (10.9–10); the world rejoices and delights in his glorification (prakīrti) (11.36).

name: Doing the Lord's work (mat-karma)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: If unable even in practice, be intent on work for the Lord (matkarmaparama); even doing actions for his sake one attains perfection (12.10). 'One who does my work (matkarmakṛt), holds me highest, is devoted to me, free from attachment and without enmity toward any being comes to me' (11.55).

name: Cultivating sameness (samatva)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Being even in understanding everywhere (12.4); the same in pain and pleasure (12.13), toward enemy and friend, in honour and dishonour, cold and heat (12.18), in blame and praise (12.19) — marks of the worshipper of the imperishable and of the devotee dear to the Lord.

name: Constant remembrance of the Lord (smaraṇa)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: the wise have their thought (citta) on the Lord and their life-breaths gone into him (10.9); the most yoked fix (āveśya) their mind (manas) on him and worship him, ever yoked, with supreme faith (12.2); 'place your mind on me alone, let your understanding (buddhi) enter into me; you will dwell in me thereafter' (12.8) — the first and highest of the graded means of 12.8–11; the devotee dear to him has mind and understanding offered to him (12.14).

name: Obeisance and adoration (vandana)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Arjuna bows his head to the Lord with joined palms (11.14); does homage trembling and bowing low (11.35); offers homage a thousand times, in front, behind and on every side (11.39–40); and, bowing and prostrating his body, seeks the Lord's grace and forgiveness (11.44).

name: Contemplating the Lord in his manifestations (vibhūti)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Asking how he may know the Lord while constantly contemplating him, Arjuna asks in which beings and states the Lord is to be thought of (10.17). The Lord names himself as the self in all beings and as the chief of each class of gods, seers, beings, things, sounds, times and qualities (10.20–39), and gives a rule for all else: whatever being is glorious or mighty is to be known as sprung from a portion of his splendour (10.41). Whoever knows his manifestation and yoga in truth is joined with unwavering yoga (10.7).
notes: New practice for 10.17–41, combining extractor A's prc:vibhuti-cintana and extractor B's prc:contemplating-the-lord-in-his-vibhutis. The text does not name it as a technique; it is implied by Arjuna's question (cintya, paricintayan, 10.17) and the rule of 10.41, and the text gives no further procedure.
